page_title: KINGAI Global Intelligence — Compare Countries, Risk & Evidence
hero_title: Understand a country before the headline.
hero_text: Compare safety, wellbeing, rights, governance and current risk under the same rules. Then follow the evidence and see what is still uncertain.
score_note: Scores appear only when source coverage and validation requirements are met. Missing values stay missing rather than being guessed.
transparent_by_design: SEE HOW THE CONCLUSION WAS BUILT
methodology_text: AI can classify, summarize and compare evidence, but measured country scores come from versioned rules and attributable datasets. The same core rules apply to every country.
principle_1_text: Unknown data stays unknown instead of being guessed.
principle_2_text: Public metrics can carry source, date and methodology metadata so you can check where a number came from.
principle_3_text: China, the United States and every other country are evaluated under the same core framework.
evidence_coverage_title: How complete is the public evidence?
evidence_coverage_note: This score measures evidence availability and source breadth only. It is not a score of country quality, truth, safety, freedom or human rights.
ooni_disclaimer: Anomalies are investigation signals, not automatic proof of censorship or government responsibility.
assessment_disclaimer: Publisher scores and reports are attributed to their original sources. Government responses are shown separately. KINGAI does not turn one source into a factual verdict.
no_assessments: No attributed assessments in the current snapshot.
discourse_disclaimer: These items are unverified public discourse. They may be false, coordinated, satirical or advocacy-driven and have direct score weight 0.

country_media_note: Only media items with an explicit country link are included here. Publisher nationality alone is never used to infer the country being discussed.
